reason: The quotes exist and the core gap is real: WAGR-449 step 3 and the WAGR-495 gate name only Kobi/Taryn as matrix reviewers, and WAGR-496 says 'approved' without naming WagerTech. But the second half of the claim is weak. The 2026-07-15 screenshot markup request was replaced on 2026-07-22 (L1232) by WagerTech flagging rep-visible fields in the feedback document. That feedback reached Jira (WAGR-278 'Rep-facing field cleanup', source 'Wagertech Additional User Stories, July 2026 item 28', Done; WAGR-348; WAGR-392 from client feedback). WAGR-495 uses Jira as its requirement source, so it does take in the client's field input. What is left is a process gap: no client sign-off step on the matrix.
q1: Found. Both quotes match verbatim with whitespace normalized. 17 Jun 2026 Discovery Session 1 (doc 1lK3Fxz..., line 485, Kobi). 15 Jul 2026 Weekly Sync (doc 1Grl2_T..., line 798, Kobi; Lina follows after a short interjection, about lines 810-812).
q2: Mostly supported. 17 Jun: the context is the access tiers (BA, brand manager, ops, exec view-only). Kobi says 'we'll put together the proposal that we can decide on', which implies a joint decision, but it is early and vague. 15 Jul: Kobi asks WagerTech to mark each field by persona and read/write. Emily replies 'we'll prioritize like doing that review and feedback'. This is a real ask that the client accepted. It is not a decision about how the matrix gets approved.
q3: Later meetings change part of the claim. L1117 (2026-07-17): first nail the signup at the rep permission level. L1232 (2026-07-22): WagerTech will identify rep-visible fields in the feedback document; this replaced the screenshot markup method. L1347 (2026-07-28): ops keep edit access on signup for now (Lina's call), so client access decisions are made in meetings. L2319 (2026-09-01): commission field visibility by role decided with the client. L3016 (2026-09-24, internal): full permissions review before go-live. L3314 (2026-09-30): permission-related signup feedback items will be done in one pass. No later meeting records a client sign-off step on the matrix.
q4: Partly covered. WAGR-449 (Epic, Open, unassigned, 0 comments): the plan's approval step is 'Kobi / Taryn review and approve the matrix'; there is no WagerTech step. WAGR-495 (Open, unassigned, 0 comments): 'Use Jira as the source of business requirements'; conflicts are flagged for Kobi/Taryn review; the gate needs review and approval but does not say by whom. WAGR-496 (Open, 0 comments): 'approved access matrix' with no approver named. The client field feedback is tracked in other tickets: WAGR-278 (Done, source: WagerTech Additional User Stories July 2026 item 28), WAGR-348 (Hide Partner from rep views, Done), WAGR-392 (brand manager visibility, from client feedback, Ready), WAGR-494, WAGR-508. JQL searches run: parent = WAGR-449 / 'access matrix' / 'persona'; 'rep visible fields' / 'feedback document' / 'field visibility' / 'sign-off permissions' / 'UAT access'.
corrections: Remove or narrow the claim that no ticket tracks the client's field markup. The markup method changed on 2026-07-22 (L1232) to the feedback document, and those items reached Jira (for example WAGR-278, WAGR-348, WAGR-392).
Add WAGR-496 as the ticket where the approver should be named. Its acceptance criteria say 'approved access matrix' but do not say who approves it.
Suggested action is still valid in narrower form: add a WagerTech review/sign-off step (Emily/Lina/Joyce) to WAGR-495 or WAGR-496 before deploy.
